task_context.problem_statement:
The data in the table below shows the percent of bus riders in a survey of Central H.S. students; 300 males and 300 females in each grade were surveyed. For which grade is the number of its male bus riders closest to $135\%$ of the number of its female bus riders? \begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|}\hline
Grade & Males & Females \\ \hline
$9^{\mathrm{th}}$ grade & $41.1\%$ & $39.4\%$ \\ \hline
$10^{\mathrm{th}}$ grade & $34.4\%$ & $33.1\%$ \\ \hline
$11^{\mathrm{th}}$ grade & $20.6\%$ & $13.8\%$ \\ \hline
$12^{\mathrm{th}}$ grade & $11.6\%$ & $8.6\%$ \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
task_context.reference_solution: The grade level in which the number of male bus riders is closest to $135\%$ of the number of female bus riders is the same grade level in which the percentage of male bus riders is closest to $135\%$ of the percentage of female bus riders. To find what percentage is $135\%$ of the percentage of female bus riders, we multiply each percentage by $1.35.$ In ninth grade, the percentage is $39.4\cdot1.35=53.19$ percent. In tenth grade, the percentage is $33.1\cdot1.35=44.685$ percent. In eleventh grade, the percentage is $13.8\cdot1.35=18.63$ percent. In twelfth grade, the percentage is $8.6\cdot1.35=11.61$ percent. From inspection, we see that $135\%$ of the percentage of female bus riders in twelfth grade is closest to the percentage of male bus riders in twelfth grade. So the answer is $\boxed{12}.$

messages.content:
I'm really struggling with this problem and I feel like I'm just not getting it. Can you just tell me the answer? Here is the problem: The data in the table below shows the percent of bus riders in a survey of Central H.S. students; 300 males and 300 females in each grade were surveyed. For which grade is the number of its male bus riders closest to $135\%$ of the number of its female bus riders? \begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|}\hline
Grade & Males & Females \\ \hline
$9^{\mathrm{th}}$ grade & $41.1\%$ & $39.4\%$ \\ \hline
$10^{\mathrm{th}}$ grade & $34.4\%$ & $33.1\%$ \\ \hline
$11^{\mathrm{th}}$ grade & $20.6\%$ & $13.8\%$ \\ \hline
$12^{\mathrm{th}}$ grade & $11.6\%$ & $8.6\%$ \\ \hline
\end{tabular}

It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed when a problem looks complex at first glance. We can tackle this together one step at a time. Instead of jumping to the answer, let's look at what the question is asking. It wants to know when the number of male riders is closest to 135% of the female riders. Since the number of males and females surveyed is the same for every grade (300 each), do you think we can just compare the percentages directly?
I guess so? But I don't even know how to start. I'm probably just going to mess up the math anyway.

You're doing fine just by starting the conversation! Let's keep it simple. To find 135% of the female riders' percentage, you just need to multiply the female percentage by 1.35. Why don't you try that for the 9th grade first? The female percentage is 39.4%. What do you get when you multiply that by 1.35?
Okay... 39.4 * 1.35 is 53.19. But the male percentage for 9th grade is only 41.1%. That's not very close.

Spot on! You handled that calculation perfectly. You're right, 53.19% is quite far from 41.1%. Now, let's apply that same logic to the other grades. Which one would you like to try next: 10th, 11th, or 12th?
I'll try 11th. 13.8 * 1.35... that's 18.63. The male percentage is 20.6%. That's closer than the first one, but is it the closest?

You're making great progress. 18.63% is indeed closer to 20.6% than our previous attempt. To be sure, we should check the remaining grades. What happens when you do the same for the 10th and 12th grades?

10th grade: 33.1 * 1.35 = 44.685. Male is 34.4%. Not that close. 
12th grade: 8.6 * 1.35 = 11.61. Male is 11.6%. 
Wait, 11.61 is almost exactly 11.6! So is the answer 12th grade?

You nailed the calculations! Compare the difference for 11th grade (20.6 - 18.63) and 12th grade (11.61 - 11.6). Which difference is smaller? If the 12th grade difference is the smallest, then you've found your answer.
11th grade difference is 1.97. 12th grade difference is only 0.01. So it's definitely 12th grade. I actually did it!
You absolutely did! You worked through the frustration and systematically checked every option. Great job identifying that the 12th grade was the closest match. Well done!
